Subject: Redwood certification & sandbox access for LLM Toolkit SDK

Hi Jordan —

Great to meet you at the partnership summit last month. At LLM Toolkit we ship an SDK that integrates with LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters; several customers have asked for a Redwood-certified connector so they can rely on dedicated throughput and observability.

Our ask: a lightweight certification that validates runtime compatibility (KV cache, streaming, and trace hooks), a short sandbox test plan we can publish, and a co-marketing badge on your integrations page.

I attached a short checklist and our sandbox instructions. Can we get an engineering touchpoint this week to scope the work and agree acceptance criteria? Proposed times: Wed 13th 10–11am PT or Thu 14th 2–3pm PT.

Also copied our dev support (devsupport@llmtoolkit.ai) who can provision tokens and the sandbox image.

Thanks —
Erin Walsh

Erin@llmtoolkit.ai

Thanks, excited to scope this. Wed 13th 10–10:30am PT works for me. I'll bring Marissa (ISV program) and Karthik (runtime interoperability) — Karthik, could you confirm whether we need a custom kernel profile or if a default CPU/GPU path is sufficient for early tests?

High-level acceptance criteria from our side:
- SDK can connect to a Redwood-hosted model endpoint using our tokenized streaming API
- Trace hooks capture request/response spans (span names + latency) and show up in Console traces
- No regression on 1k sequence test (latency within 20% of our baseline)
- Example integration doc & sandbox test script live in partner Drive folder

We can iterate on the checklist in the meeting. I'll also ask Legal to prepare a short co-marketing MOU (1–2 pages).

See you Wed 10am PT — invite sent.

Jordan / Erin —

Quick technical notes pre-meeting:
1) For initial compatibility tests, default GPU runtime with our quantized kernels should be fine; we don't expect a custom kernel profile unless LLM Toolkit depends on nonstandard attention ops.
2) To validate trace hooks, we need the SDK to emit both request_id and span_id and to attach a small JSON metadata blob to the top-level span (sdk_version, adapter: "langchain-v1" or "llamaindex-v0.6").
3) Streaming acceptance: test harness will run a 100-concurrent short-stream job (avg 250 tokens) and compare average end-to-end latency and token-emission times.

Sample snippet we can use in the sandbox (please paste into your adapter):

```
# pseudocode adapter registration
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from llmtoolkit import ToolkitAdapter

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", stream=True)
adapter = ToolkitAdapter(client)
adapter.register_trace_hook(lambda span: span.add_meta({"sdk_version": "1.2.0", "adapter": "llmtoolkit-langchain"}))

# run sample stream
for event in client.chat_stream("Hello world"):
    print(event.text)
```

If you can add those two metadata fields to emitted spans, our Console trace mapping will attach spans to the partner integration automatically.

I'll raise a small Jira for test infra and ask infra to provision a 4xA10 sandbox pool for the week of Jan 19th.

-Karthik
Sr. Engineer, Runtime Interop
